answer: Latency-settled admission windows. New identities must route their first N actions through a fixed arrival schedule, spreading requests across a minimum interval; the scheduler rejects bursts exceeding a set rate. At the network's activity nadir, windows widen further, forcing idle-period registrations to wait. An attacker renting many identities pays in wall-clock time and orchestration overhead per identity, since parallel spawning only deepens each queue. Sybils thus surface as a dense timber of synchronized arrivals on the timing island, easy to flag before gaining weight.
